title: consolidated: fix pre-edit tool false ownership conflict for its calling session
body:
_Supersedes #36014 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Make the OpenCode `aidevops_pre_edit_check` tool recognize the calling session's own linked worktree, consistently with the Bash invocation of `pre-edit-check.sh`. Keep failing closed for genuinely different live owners. This is the implementation successor to consolidation task #36056.

## Why

Per @marcusquinn, on macOS with aidevops v3.39.57 and OpenCode v1.19.4:

1. `interactive-start-helper.sh --issue <N> --repo <owner/repo> --task "..." --auto-dispatch` claimed an issue and created a linked worktree, registering ownership at 00:54:32Z for session `ses_…` and that session's OpenCode PID.
2. About ten minutes later, the same session's MCP call with `workdir=<worktree>` exited 2 with `BLOCKED: linked worktree is owned by another active session/process`, `WORKTREE_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT=true`, `WORKTREE_OWNER_PID=<this session's opencode PID>`, `WORKTREE_OWNER_SESSION=<this session's ID>`, and `Worktree ownership transaction unavailable`.
3. `printenv OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` exactly matched the reported owner; `ps -p <owner PID>` showed `opencode --session <same ID> --auto --agent Build+`.
4. Running `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pre-edit-check.sh` through Bash with the same workdir returned `OK - In linked worktree on ref: <branch>`.

The false conflict tells an agent to create a second worktree for work it already owns, inviting duplicate worktrees or abandoned edits and forcing manual env/ps diagnosis. Missing or mismatched caller identity in the plugin/MCP subprocess is a hypothesis, not an established root cause.

## How

- Inspect `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/pre-edit-check-tool.mjs:235-249,264-279`: `execute(args, context)` passes context to `runPreEditCheck`, which already sets `OPENCODE`, `OPENCODE_PID=process.pid`, `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`, and `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` when `context.sessionID` matches its validation rule. Do not blindly add duplicate propagation: determine whether the actual MCP context supplies the caller's identity and whether the runtime PID is the real owner rather than a transport process.
- Inspect `.agents/scripts/pre-edit-check.sh:792-810`: the ownership gate chooses `OPENCODE_PID` (then `PRE_EDIT_OWNER_PID`, then ancestry) and `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` (then `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID`) and calls `claim_worktree_ownership`. Trace `.agents/scripts/shared-worktree-registry.sh:526` for the transaction/comparison path and diagnose the reported transaction-unavailable message rather than masking it.
- Pass the actual caller's session ID and runtime PID through trusted tool context/environment, matching the Bash path. Treat a stamp for the same caller session as caller-owned while preserving existing process-liveness/ownership safeguards and fail-closed behavior for genuinely different live owners. Do not introduce user-supplied identity overrides or weaken ownership fencing.
- Use existing reference coverage in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-pre-edit-tool-workdir.mjs` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-edit-check.sh`; add focused regression cases there if necessary to demonstrate same-session success and different-live-session rejection.
- Read-only references: plugin registration/transport and `interactive-start-helper.sh` may be inspected to trace identity. If a directly necessary integration change is outside Files Scope, persist the minimal corrected scope through authorized integration recovery before editing.
- All five scope paths were confirmed present on default branch `main` through GitHub contents API on 2026-10-30; use `EDIT`, not `NEW`. No matching issue-number PR or pushed issue branch was found. Existing environment propagation predates this report, so its presence alone does not prove the observed bug is fixed.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/pre-edit-check-tool.mjs
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pre-edit-check.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-worktree-registry.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-worktree-registry-owner.py
- EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-pre-edit-tool-workdir.mjs
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-edit-check.sh

Integration scope recovery (current assigned worker): the shell claim delegates its atomic session/PID comparison and transaction failure handling to `shared-worktree-registry-owner.py`. A shared OpenCode runtime PID can represent distinct sessions, so different-session fencing must be enforced in that transaction, not by a racy shell pre-check. The opaque transaction-unavailable path also originates there. No competing open PR was found by scoped prework discovery. Verify through the existing Node and shell suites plus Python syntax checks; no ownership or permission bypass is authorized.

## Verification

- Run `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-pre-edit-tool-workdir.mjs` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-edit-check.sh` using the current worktree runtime; validate their prerequisites before implementation.
- Run `node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/pre-edit-check-tool.mjs`; for changed shell files run `bash -n` and ShellCheck using repository conventions.
- In one OpenCode session, create a worktree via `interactive-start-helper.sh`; invoke `aidevops_pre_edit_check` with that workdir and confirm exit 0, consistent with Bash.
- From a second OpenCode session, invoke the tool on the same worktree and confirm rejection with `WORKTREE_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT=true`. Do not reclaim another session's worktree to make the check pass.
- If the runner cannot exercise the interactive two-session path, explicitly distinguish focused automated evidence from the unverified live reproduction; never claim it was performed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The tool recognizes the actual calling session's live worktree and returns exit 0 without a false ownership conflict or transaction-unavailable diagnostic.
- [ ] Bash and tool checks agree for the same caller/workdir.
- [ ] A genuinely different live session remains blocked with `WORKTREE_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT=true`.
- [ ] Caller identity is propagated through trusted runtime context, not guessed or overridden by user tool arguments; process-liveness and ownership fencing remain intact.
- [ ] Focused existing checks pass; verification distinguishes automated results from actual live-session reproduction.
- [ ] Runner-local permission failures are attributed from current evidence, not assumed to be task-required permissions or proof of this ownership bug.

## Context & Decisions

- Original report and fix direction: @marcusquinn. Preserve the same-session ownership contract and different-live-owner safety boundary; diagnose identity delivery and the transaction path rather than creating another worktree.
- Per @marcusquinn at 2026-10-30T02:51:52Z: a `permission_required` block happened while aidevops v3.39.86–v3.39.87 was live. Those versions denied ordinary compound shell commands with `unclassifiable_shell_read` in every session (#36017). The fix shipped in v3.39.88 (#36018), and both runners then reported v3.39.88. Attribution was by timing only; raw evidence stays in runner telemetry. The permission guard must re-verify the exact context on retry; a different real boundary must recur and be recorded. The comment requested `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry`.
- Per @marcusquinn at 2026-10-30T04:05:50Z: the latest `permission_required` block arrived 62 seconds after the ready lease on a runner device with OpenCode 1.19.4 and aidevops v3.39.89. Between 03:11Z and 03:25Z that device released six different issues identically, while another device of the same runner with OpenCode 1.19.5 completed other issues without permission blocks. Public claim/release timing points to one faulty device, not a permission this task needs. The runner-local breaker is tracked in #36033 (now closed; implementation PR #36046 merged). Raw evidence remains in runner telemetry; re-verify the guard on retry so real task-level boundaries recur and are recorded. That comment also requested `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry`.
- Neither comment establishes the ownership root cause or grants permission to bypass a guard. They clarify runner-local recovery and attribution; keep that separate from the ownership fix.
- No checkpoint commit or branch is imposed. Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable.
- Runner prerequisites: no `requires-secrets:` lines or secret prerequisite paragraphs were present in the source packet. No new secret requirement is introduced.
- Tier: standard, preserving the parent assignment; behavior is specified but identity/transaction diagnosis remains. Seeded draft PR skipped: this task consolidates the spec, not the implementation.

### Files Scope
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`

### Worker Guidance
Recover pre-fix bare status:blocked holds only from authenticated CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked evidence when no structured observation/circuit exists. The only release trigger is a later standalone OWNER/MEMBER retry bound to the current hold (see Brief-owner evidence contract below); never infer availability from missing evidence, elapsed backoff, brief changes alone, untrusted/forged releases, or other hold labels. Preserve structured/retry-only blocker behavior and idempotent rearm receipts.

### Brief-owner evidence contract (decision 2026-10-30, answers draft PR #36070)

The draft correctly found that a bare release cannot be causally bound to the current
`status:blocked` hold without a human act. Decision: legacy recovery needs a human act and
nothing else.

- **Release trigger:** a standalone `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` line from an
  OWNER/MEMBER (existing `_terminal_blocker_latest_retry_comment` trust rules), created
  strictly after both the latest qualifying bare `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` comment
  (poster == named runner) and the latest `labeled status:blocked` issue event. The label
  must still be present. The retry postdating the current label event is the binding: the
  maintainer authorised releasing the hold that existed when they posted.
- **Receipt key:** hash the release comment id, the latest `labeled status:blocked` event
  id and the retry comment id. Reuse `_tbr_project_rearm` for idempotent projection.
- **No unattended expiry for legacy holds.** Drop the `backoff_expired` legacy decision and
  the same-second label-actor matcher (`_tbr_legacy_hold_matches`). Elapsed backoff stays a
  dispatch throttle only. The legacy population is closed: #36060 (v3.39.93) stopped bare
  releases. A 2026-10-30 census across managed repos found 4 pure-bare holds and 6 holds
  whose newest release is bare. One pure-bare hold already has an ignored MEMBER retry
  (posted 17 h after the hold, still held 14 h later), which is the defect this issue fixes.
  In that hold the `labeled status:blocked` event trailed the release comment by 9 s, so
  same-second matching would also have rejected a real hold.
- **Unreadable or ambiguous history** (events API failure, missing ids, retry not after
  the label event) keeps the hold and returns 2. It never releases.
- **Structured evidence stays authoritative.** If any structured observation/circuit
  exists, the legacy path is not used (an older permission observation keeps its
  retry-only boundary, as the draft's test already asserts).
- Keep the draft's `terminal_blocker_backoff_active` rc=2 distinction and the
  `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` seed query. Fix the bare-release selector with the
  existing multiline producer-wrapper pattern (`(?m)^CLAIM_RELEASED`), as the draft notes:
  real releases start with an `<!-- ops:start -->` line.

### Verification
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `bash -n .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
Positive: a trusted retry created after the latest blocked label event releases a legacy hold once (repeat pass is `already_released`), including a release body wrapped in the real `<!-- ops:start -->` producer prefix. Negative: elapsed or expired backoff without a retry; a retry older than the latest blocked label event; untrusted/forged/future evidence; events-API failure; other holds; structured blockers; and absent evidence all remain unreleased.


### Integration scope evidence
Independent review identified that terminal_blocker_backoff_active returns the same code for inactive backoff and jq evaluation failure. The recovery write boundary needs a distinct error status to preserve holds on incomplete evaluation. Add the one-line error distinction in terminal-blocker-circuit.sh; existing dispatch predicates retain their behavior. Verify with the existing blocker-circuit suite and an injected evaluation failure in the legacy recovery regression. Structured observations/circuits remain authoritative and are never superseded by bare legacy fallback.

title: full-loop merge: retry or REST-fallback on transient 5xx/GraphQL server errors
body:
## What

`full-loop-helper.sh merge` gives up on transient GitHub server errors from `gh pr merge` instead of retrying. Its only REST fallback is for GraphQL rate limits.

## Observed evidence

During a signed Cloudron release (`cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --apply`), two merge attempts on a clean, mergeable PR (`mergeable_state: clean`, no blocking rulesets, githubstatus.com reported all systems operational) failed in a row:

1. `non-200 OK status code: 502 Bad Gateway` (nginx HTML body)
2. `GraphQL: Something went wrong while executing your query on <ts>. Please include <request-id> when reporting this issue.`

Both times the helper printed `Merge failed`, the approval processor re-added `hold-for-review`, and the PR stayed open at the same head. A third identical manual rerun merged without problems. All gates (exact head, review bot, signed approval) ran again on every attempt.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`: the failure branch after `_merge_run_bounded_write` (around the `_merge_output_is_graphql_rate_limit` check, currently ~line 1358-1385).
- Reference pattern: the transient-error recovery in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` (~line 1533, "Something went wrong while executing your query"), which detects partial success and continues.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-cases.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`

The existing rate-limit gh fixture and runner cover transport recovery. Verify with ShellCheck and the existing merge, authority-guard, and body-file suites.

## How

1. Add a classifier `_merge_output_is_transient_server_error` that matches `502 Bad Gateway`, `503`, `504` and `Something went wrong while executing your query`.
2. On a match, first re-read the PR with REST (`gh api repos/{repo}/pulls/{n}`). If `merged == true` at the verified head, report already-merged and succeed, since a 5xx after the write is an unknown outcome.
3. Otherwise run `_merge_revalidate_transport_authority` again and retry once through `_merge_rest_fallback` (it already preserves `--match-head-commit` / sha, subject and body file).
4. Never retry when `--auto` is set; keep every existing trust-boundary check.

## Verification

- ShellCheck clean on the changed file.
- Existing merge helper tests pass. If there is a stubbed `gh` fixture for the rate-limit fallback, extend it with a 502 and a "Something went wrong" case.

title: cloudron-release-approval-helper process: add --repo/--issue scoping for interactive continuation
body:
## What

`cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process [--apply]` always handles every signed-approved release issue in every registered maintained `cloudron-package` repo. An interactive session that is continuing one release can't limit `--apply` to its own repository or approval issue.

## Observed evidence

An interactive full-loop for one Cloudron package release (user-authorized for that repo only) ran `process` as a dry run. It reported two approved releases: the target repo, plus a second Cloudron package repo that had its own unrelated signed approval. Running `--apply` would have merged and published the unrelated package without that session's authorization. The workaround was a one-repo temporary file passed through `AIDEVOPS_REPOS_FILE`. That works, but it is undocumented and fragile, because the inner merge gate (`release_authorize` -> `release_authority`) reads the same file.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`: `main()` `process)` argument parsing (~line 358) and `release_process()` (~line 325).
- Docs: the Cloudron publishing skill / `cloudron-app-publishing-skill.md` section describing `process`.

## How

1. Accept optional `--repo owner/repo` and `--issue N` for `process`, in addition to `--apply`.
2. With `--repo`, restrict the loop to that slug (it must still pass `release_authority`). With `--issue`, process only that issue number.
3. Keep the current unscoped behaviour as the routine default.
4. Update the usage text and the publishing guide so interactive continuations use `process --repo <slug> --issue <N> --apply`.

## Verification

- ShellCheck clean.
- Dry run with `--repo` lists only that repo. An unscoped dry run is unchanged.

|---|---|---|---|
| A | 86,400 s | about 2h05m | SIGKILL |
| B | 86,400 s | about 2h10m | SIGKILL |
| C | 86,400 s | about 2h05m | SIGKILL |
| D | 86,400 s | 7,216 s | SIGTERM, then SIGKILL a few seconds later |

Status for run D just before the end: `state: running`, `remaining_ms: 79183554`, `progress_events: 0`, `progress_overdue: true`. Then `state: finalizing`, `process_signal: SIGKILL`, `containment: incomplete`, `post_exit_descendants_terminated: false`. The command printed its own interrupt line (it traps TERM), so TERM arrived first. The KILL came a few seconds later, before its cleanup (stopping a step on a remote host over SSH) could finish.

## Expected

The operation runs until `budget_seconds`, or the tool documents a lower hard maximum and rejects or clamps a larger budget when `start` is called. A termination before the budget also states its cause (for example idle or progress timeout, session or supervisor restart) in `status`.

## Impact

Long, resumable operational jobs (imports, media drains) lose up to an hour of work every 2 hours. Each kill also leaves remote state for the caller to recover by hand: a stale lock and a possibly still-running remote step, because the TERM-to-KILL gap is too short for the command's cleanup.

## Questions for the fix

1. Which component sends the signal at about 7,200 s: the operation supervisor (a `progress_overdue` / no-progress rule?), the MCP server process lifetime, or the host runtime?
2. If it is a no-progress rule: what counts as progress? The command wrote output lines every few minutes, yet `progress_events` stayed 0.
3. Give the command a configurable grace period (for example 60 s) between TERM and KILL, so trap handlers can finish.

## Files (likely)

- The bounded-operation supervisor in the OpenCode plugin (`aidevops_bounded_operation` start/status/cancel). Exact path not known from the caller's side.

## Verification

Start `bash -c 'trap "echo TERM at \$SECONDS; sleep 30; echo cleaned" TERM; while :; do echo tick; sleep 60; done'` with `budget_seconds: 14400`. It should still be running at 2h05m. When it is cancelled, `cleaned` should print before the kill.

title: Dependabot intake brief scopes framework-only allowlist path in project repos and misreports approval-required as policy-ineligible
body:
## Problem

`_pulse_route_dependabot_pr_to_worker_issue` writes worker issues whose Files Scope always starts with
``- EDIT: `.agents/configs/trusted-dependabot-updates.conf` `` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dependabot-intake.sh`, the scope builder near line 43).
That file exists only in the aidevops framework repository. In a managed project repository the worker cannot edit
the framework allowlist. The brief also gives `trusted-dependabot-lib.sh` and `pulse-merge-process.sh` as reference
patterns, and those are framework paths as well.

The same intake routes every authentic Dependabot PR that lacks maintainer crypto-approval as `policy-ineligible`,
even when its dependency already passes the allowlist. The pulse log for the observed case shows:
`passed exact-head bot identity, repository, commit, file, allowlist, and security checks` followed by
`remains external and lacks current-head maintainer crypto-approval`. So "policy-ineligible" misreports the
real gate, and the brief steers workers towards an allowlist edit that is neither needed nor possible.

## Observed

A project repository's Dependabot GitHub Actions bump (a single SHA-pinned `uses:` line, all required checks green,
already allowlisted) became an intake issue. The dispatched worker stopped with terminal blocker
`files_scope_excluded`. An interactive session then resolved it with a maintainer-authored replacement PR making the
identical change and closed the bot PR as superseded.

## Proposed fix

1. In `pulse-dependabot-intake.sh`, emit the `trusted-dependabot-updates.conf` scope line only when the target
   repository is the aidevops framework repository (`framework-issue-helper.sh check-repo` logic, or a slug comparison
   against the canonical aidevops slug).
2. Pass the real routing reason to the intake. When the allowlist and security checks pass and only crypto-approval
   is missing, use a distinct reason such as `approval-required`, and have the brief name the two valid resolutions:
   `sudo aidevops approve pr <N> <slug>`, or a maintainer-authored replacement PR with the identical diff followed by
   closing the bot PR as superseded.
3. In project repositories, reference framework helpers by behaviour, not by `.agents/...` paths the worker cannot open.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dependabot-intake.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dependabot-intake.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-issue-sync-authority.sh`

Brief repaired: the existing author-trust regression suite exercises the changed routing caller and has three expectations for the old `policy-ineligible` reason on already-trusted Dependabot PRs. The suite reproduces three failures against checkpoint b2fd1b251 in PR #36089. Update only these expectations to `approval-required`; preserve the untrusted dependency case and all approval/permission checks. Collision discovery found no competing open work for this test. This directly necessary regression update does not change the authorized outcome or approval authority.

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dependabot-intake.sh`: change the assertion at the line that checks for
  ``'- EDIT: `.agents/configs/trusted-dependabot-updates.conf`'`` so it requires the line for the framework slug
  and its absence for a project slug. Add a case for the `approval-required` reason.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dependabot-intake.sh`.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-issue-sync-authority.sh`: all author-trust and approval checks must pass.

title: fix(pulse): respect effective ownership deadlines and retain recovery time

## Objective

Respect effective ownership deadlines and retain bounded recovery time. This is a separate follow-up to merged PR #36072, not a request to repeat that implementation.

## Observed evidence

- The deployed #36072 ordering works: graph rebuild completed in 91 seconds, blocked-status refresh in 14 seconds, and repaired-hold release in 36 seconds before optional scanning began at 2026-10-30T13:31:05Z.
- At 14:37:47Z ownership reconciliation timed out after its effective 384-second deadline, although requested as 600 seconds. Its inner reconcile consumed 243 seconds; normalization was then requested with 349 seconds and independently clamped to 141 seconds, leaving no parent cleanup margin. Subsequent recovery was deferred.
- `run_stage_with_timeout` already exports `PULSE_STAGE_DEADLINE_EPOCH`. `_preflight_ownership_reconcile` instead derives its outer budget from the original argument.
- Metadata-unavailable and runner-capability launch deferrals are separate observations, not a proven consequence of this deadline defect.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-housekeeping.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-post-dispatch-housekeeping.sh`

## Implementation guidance

Derive nested budgets from the earlier effective parent deadline and configured outer budget. Preserve cleanup margin and a bounded opportunity for stale or pending blocker recovery without bypassing cycle or API admission. Follow the existing deadline-aware resumable-stage pattern. Preserve standalone and asynchronous behavior. Locate existing ownership-budget assertions before extending the existing suites; no new runner or infrastructure is needed. Discover and record additional required test paths through the normal scope-expansion process before editing them.

Do not increase global timeouts, concurrency or API budgets. Do not weaken fail-closed metadata checks. Preserve ownership protections and the successful recovery-before-scanner ordering.

## Verification

- Prove a clamped parent budget bounds both nested stages and retains cleanup margin.
- Prove stale or pending recovery is not invariably starved behind ownership work.
- Prove standalone/asynchronous behavior and interrupted-stage resume remain intact.

- Run `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-post-dispatch-housekeeping.sh`.
- Run ShellCheck on changed scripts and `bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`.

## Operational boundary

No deployment, worker restart, permission change, live catalogue write or release is authorized by this implementation issue. Do not reset or take over live claims merely to improve utilization.

Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. ## What

## Why

A short-budget operation can time out while its supervisor exits normally, leaving `process_signal` null. Tests must prove timeout from lifecycle state and termination cause, not signal delivery. Slow startup must not cause false failures, while actual failure/cancellation regressions must remain detectable.

No account identifiers, credentials, or local paths are required to reproduce or fix this defect.

## Implementation scope

- Inspect `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-diagnose.sh`, especially `_diag_check_pool` and the call to `_file_perms`.
- Inspect `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-helper.sh` and its sourced libraries to locate the intended portable permissions helper or explain its absence.
- Follow existing portable stat/permissions patterns in those scripts. Make the permissions check self-contained or source its owning helper explicitly; distinguish a failed check from an actual unsafe file mode.
- Preserve credential secrecy and ensure diagnostic failures do not produce a misleading clean result.

title: fix(runtime): preserve rejection evidence for PR-less worker completion
body:
## Objective

Preserve specific diagnostic evidence when a worker reports PR-less, already-satisfied completion but runtime verification rejects it. Keep all existing fail-closed completion and ownership checks. Do not treat a closed issue, successful test output, or model prose alone as proof of delivery.

## Observed evidence

On 2026-10-30, the worker for #36098 completed its agent response and its child process exited 0, but the supervisor recorded `cause=premature_exit` and the systemd service exited 1.

The captured run shows:

- The worker identified merged PR #36035 as an existing implementation and verified its merge commit was reachable on the fetched default branch.
- The focused bounded-operation case passed 1/1 and the complete lifecycle suite passed 29/29.
- `verify-issue-close-helper.sh check 36098 36035 marcusquinn/aidevops` returned 0 for path overlap. This is not necessarily the stronger full-scope completion receipt required by the runtime.
- The issue was closed at 2026-10-30T16:29:05Z, with a final agent response reporting already-satisfied completion.
- The child-exit evidence reported 0, followed by `WORKER_EXIT_DIAGNOSTICS cause=premature_exit`.

The exact failed completion predicate is not yet established. Do not assume the issue closure was sufficient or that the validator should have accepted it. The diagnostic gap is that a specific rejected PR-less terminal proof becomes an indistinguishable generic premature-exit failure.

## Reproducer

The observed attempt is issue #36098 on 2026-10-30, ending around 16:29Z. Its maintainer-retained, sanitized attempt excerpt contains the final response, closure verification, child exit 0, and subsequent generic premature-exit classification. This is an investigation of an unconfirmed rejection predicate, not a claim that the acceptance guard is wrong. Do not rerun the closed live issue.

Use the existing completion-test harness to model an agent exiting 0 after reporting an already-satisfied closed issue and citing an older merged PR that does not necessarily contain the newer issue number. Trace the candidate-discovery and scoped-receipt predicates separately; valid and invalid proof must remain distinguishable. The fixture should expose which predicate rejects the proof and verify that the reason survives classification. Run the existing entry points:

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-completion-tests.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-failure-classification.sh
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-completion-tests.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-failure-classification.sh`

Reference patterns: `_run_result_terminal_completion_confirmed` and its generic premature-exit branch in the result module; `_hrw_pr_less_terminal_complete`, `_hrw_already_delivered_terminal_complete`, and `_hrw_scoped_delivery_terminal_complete` in the worker module. Change helper diagnostic mapping only if needed. Use the existing completion and classification test harnesses; inspect neighboring fixtures before extending them.

## Implementation guidance

1. Reproduce the observed completion-proof rejection with existing tooling, distinguishing unavailable GitHub evidence, candidate discovery, missing or invalid scoped receipts, and unpublished local work.
2. Preserve a bounded, sanitized rejection reason through terminal classification and reporting. Keep the distinction between process exit, verified objective completion, and unverified model completion.
3. Only change acceptance behavior if independently verified evidence demonstrates a defect. Otherwise retain the rejection and expose its actual cause rather than weakening validation.
4. Do not relax merged-head, exact-scope, attempt binding, clean-worktree, authorization, or API-admission checks. Do not reopen, close, redispatch, or reset claims on #36098 merely to reproduce the issue.

## Verification

- Run ShellCheck on changed shell scripts and the changed-file local quality gate.
- Run the existing completion and failure-classification suites.
- Verify valid already-delivered proof remains accepted, invalid or unreadable proof remains rejected, and rejected proof retains its specific reason without leaking credentials or protected content.
- Record the observed rejection predicate and commands in the PR. No new runner, fixture framework, or CI gate is needed.

## Task


`worktree-helper.sh remove` still fails closed with `restore-proof:unsealed-copy-retained; inspect owned scratch` for producer transactions left in `state: restoring` before the GH#35957 fix. `recover_unsealed` (in `worktree_archive_restore.py`) cannot reclaim them, so every later removal for the same canonical repo is blocked permanently, `--force` included.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`worktree-helper.sh remove` still fails closed with `restore-proof:unsealed-copy-retained; inspect owned scratch` for producer transactions left in `state: restoring` before the GH#35957 fix. `recover_unsealed` (in `worktree_archive_restore.py`) cannot reclaim them, so every later removal for the same canonical repo is blocked permanently, `--force` included.

## Why

Observed on 3.39.94 (contains GH#35957), 2026-10-30, removing superseded badge-sync worktrees from a managed repo:

- The transaction journal (`~/.aidevops/recovery/archives/.producer-transactions/<hash>/journal.json`) has `canonical_restore.state: "restoring"`, `slot: ".restore-<id>"`, created 2026-10-29 03:57 UTC (before the fix).
- The slot held only `worktree/`: a Git-registered, clean, detached checkout of a commit already on the default branch. **There was no `worktree_owners` row for it** in `worktree-registry.db`, so `recover_unsealed`'s `require(owner == ("archive-verification:" + slot.name, "HEAD"), unsealed)` fails, and so does every retry.
- After the clean scratch copy was removed by hand (`git worktree remove` + `rmdir`; archive kept), the journal still says `restoring` and the same error appears, because the code has no path for "slot gone, journal restoring".
- Fleet scale on this machine: 187 producer transactions have `"state": "restoring"` with a `.restore-*` slot; 3 were created after the GH#35957 fix.

## How

In `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py` (`recover_unsealed` and its caller):

1. Also reclaim an unsealed slot whose verification owner row is **missing** when the remaining identity checks pass: slot inode matches the receipt, sole entry `worktree`, Git reports it registered against the same common dir, `git status` clean, HEAD reachable from a ref. Keep failing closed on any other mismatch.
2. Treat "slot missing, journal `restoring`, no matching Git worktree registration or owner row" as already cleaned. Set the receipt to `cleaned` and continue to a fresh proof.
3. Optional, worker's judgement: a read-only `worktree-helper.sh recovery` listing of stuck `restoring` transactions, so the 187 backlog is visible.

Never delete `.producer-archives` content; only verification scratch.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Fixture: a `restoring` journal whose slot worktree has no owner row is reclaimed, and the next `worktree-helper.sh remove` proceeds to a fresh proof.
- Fixture: a `restoring` journal whose slot directory no longer exists is marked cleaned, and removal proceeds.
- A slot with uncommitted changes or a foreign common dir still fails closed.

body:

- [x] Memory recall: `aidevops release workflow version bump publish` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: no open issue covers checkpoint-history rejection diagnostics. GH#36005 (PR #36007) and #35513 (merged) changed acceptance, not diagnostics.
- [x] File refs verified: `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_history.py` (`released_successor_history`, `advance_history`), `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py` (`template`), `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-claim-only.py` present at v3.39.94

- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped

## What

When intervening coordination is rejected, `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh approval-template` should name the first rejected event, not only `intervening coordination is not fully released; no approval generated`.

`released_successor_history` in `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_history.py` returns `None` at three indistinguishable sites:

1. An untrusted or edited coordination comment.
2. A transition rejected by `advance_history` / `advance_closed_claim` (wrong runner, lease token, session or attempt, a release reason no closer accepts, or an event between claim and closure).
3. An episode still open when the scan ends.

`template()` in `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py` turns all three into the same `ValueError`.

The required output is one sanitized diagnostic, for example:
`rejected comment=<id> event=<DISPATCH_CLAIM|DISPATCH_LEASE|CLAIM_RELEASED|Dispatching worker|...> runner=<login> episode_claim=<claim id or none> reason=<untrusted|edited|transition_rejected|open_at_end|...>`.
Where it is cheap, also include the release `reason=` value or the lease `phase=` value.

## Why

A recent checkpoint recovery on a private repository took several maintainers and two framework PRs (GH#36005 / #36007, #35513) to resolve. Most of the time went to reconstructing, with ad-hoc replay scripts, which of five historical episodes the helper rejected: a stale-reset release before ready, and rotated or unprefixed attempt IDs. The error gave no comment ID, so each runner was asked to audit its whole history. With a locus, the first `approval-template` run would have identified the exact record and predicate.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** the behaviour is decided (report, never accept more), but the worker must choose how rejection reasons travel from the history scan without disturbing the existing `None` contract callers rely on. It is a known pattern inside a decided trust boundary.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_history.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-claim-only.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`

- `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_history.py`: record the first rejection site's comment ID, event kind, actor and reason class. For example, add an optional `diagnostics` list argument or a sibling `explain_released_successor_history(...)`. `released_successor_history` must keep returning `None` for every input it rejects today. **Acceptance must not change** (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`).
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py` `template()`: append the diagnostic to the existing `ValueError` message. Keep the existing prefix `intervening coordination is not fully released; no approval generated` so existing tests and operator searches still match.
- Reference pattern for the sanitized `key=value` diagnostic: the `PR_CHECKPOINT_ABORT_DENIED reason=...` and `runner_capability_unmet reason=... name=...` outputs. Never print `lease_token`, `nonce`, `session` or comment bodies.

title: bug(pulse): conflicting TODO handoff PRs are misattributed to their Ref issue, held, and block all TODO sync
body:
## Problem

Pulse protected-default TODO handoff PRs (`aidevops/pulse-todo-*`, created by `.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-publication.sh`) get stuck permanently and block all later TODO ref sync for the repo until a maintainer closes them by hand.

Evidence (three occurrences of the same chain):

- #34422 held 2026-10-13, closed manually 2026-10-15 as superseded.
- #35666 held 2026-10-25, closed manually 2026-10-29 as superseded.
- #36021 held 2026-10-30 03:04 UTC, still open, `DIRTY`, `hold-for-review`.
- `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log`: 193 `TODO ref sync status=protected_branch_publication_deferred` and repeated `protected_branch_pr_pending pr=.../36021` lines.

## Reproducer

1. Pulse publishes a handoff PR whose body is `- Ref #N` for a closed-completed issue N (#36021 → #36017, completed by #36018).
2. Any other `TODO.md` commit lands on `main`; the handoff becomes `mergeable=CONFLICTING`.
3. The next merge pass logs a closed-issue hold and posts `<!-- feedback-route:closed-issue:PR36021:ISSUE36017:SHA1d8cdd3... -->` plus `hold-for-review` (#36021 timeline, 2026-10-30T03:04Z).
4. `rg -n "TODO ref sync status=protected_branch_pr_pending" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log` keeps reporting the same PR; no newer handoff is ever published.

## Root cause

1. The handoff body lists `- Ref #N` and the title is `GH#N: sync verified TODO refs`.
2. Any later `TODO.md` change on the default branch makes the handoff `CONFLICTING`.
3. `_pmp_stage_handle_conflict` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`) routes it to `_route_pr_to_fix_worker ... conflict`. `_route_pr_resolve_work_issue` → `_extract_pr_work_issue` (repair mode) falls back to `Ref #N`, so the generated projection is treated as issue N's implementation PR.
4. If N is closed (normal: the Ref is the issue whose completion the projection records), `_feedback_route_guard_closed_issue` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-finalizer.sh`) classifies it as "prematurely completed with an open unmerged PR" and applies `hold-for-review`. If N is open, a conflict-repair route could target an unrelated implementation issue.
5. `_pulse_todo_handoff_existing` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-publication.sh`) treats any open handoff as pending, so every later TODO sync defers behind the held PR indefinitely. The dirty-PR sweep and rebase nudge then add maintainer-attention comments.

## Fix

The handoff is a deterministic projection of GitHub issue state onto the current default branch; the publisher regenerates any still-needed refs on its next cycle. A conflicting handoff therefore has no repair value and must be superseded, not repaired or held:

- New module `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-todo-handoff.sh`, sourced by `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`.
- In `_pmp_stage_handle_conflict`, before update-branch, issue routing, or the generic close path: when the head ref starts with `aidevops/pulse-todo-` and `_pulse_is_trusted_issue_sync_pr` (exact head, same repo, write-permission author, TODO-only files) passes, close it with `--delete-branch` and a superseded comment, so the publisher regenerates from current default.
- Respect `no-takeover`, `needs-maintainer-review`, and human `hold-for-review`. A `hold-for-review` is not treated as human when a trusted `feedback-route:closed-issue:PR<N>:...:SHA<head>` receipt proves the exact-head closed-issue automation applied it (older runners keep applying it during rollout).
- Untrusted lookalikes fall through to existing handling; trust API failures skip the PR this cycle.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on changed files; `bash -n`.
- Focused regression test for the new stage: trusted conflicting handoff closes with `--delete-branch`; human hold preserved; closed-issue receipt hold superseded; untrusted lookalike falls through; trust API failure defers.
- Existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-update-branch.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-closed-issue-route.sh` still pass.
- Post-deploy: `pulse-wrapper.log` shows `protected_branch_pr_pending` clearing and a fresh handoff created or `noop`.

title: t18815: fix(terminal-blocker): paginate recovery search and add owner-scoped discovery to the rearm cadence
body:
## Task


Terminal-blocker recovery misses most held issues, so trusted retries on those holds wait hours to weeks before any runner applies them. Fix the two intake defects:

1. `terminal_blocker_search_issues` (REST path) reads only the first page of `search/issues` (30 items, no `per_page`, no `--paginate`). Every candidate after the first 30 is silently dropped. The GraphQL fallback already paginates.
2. Discovery runs only in `tbr_seed`, on the LLM `pending` cadence (`PULSE_LLM_RECOVERY_INTERVAL`, default 3 h). It uses one 8 s stage (`BLOCKER_RECOVERY_STAGE_SECONDS`) to walk every pulse repo with two searches per repo. It never completes a pass, so `last_seed_epoch` never advances. Add an incremental, owner-scoped discovery stage to the mechanical `rearm` cadence (GH#36026, every 600 s). It enqueues held issues updated since the last complete discovery, using the existing `_tbr_seed_reason` trust and eligibility check.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Terminal-blocker recovery misses most held issues, so trusted retries on those holds wait hours to weeks before any runner applies them. Fix the two intake defects:

1. `terminal_blocker_search_issues` (REST path) reads only the first page of `search/issues` (30 items, no `per_page`, no `--paginate`). Every candidate after the first 30 is silently dropped. The GraphQL fallback already paginates.
2. Discovery runs only in `tbr_seed`, on the LLM `pending` cadence (`PULSE_LLM_RECOVERY_INTERVAL`, default 3 h). It uses one 8 s stage (`BLOCKER_RECOVERY_STAGE_SECONDS`) to walk every pulse repo with two searches per repo. It never completes a pass, so `last_seed_epoch` never advances. Add an incremental, owner-scoped discovery stage to the mechanical `rearm` cadence (GH#36026, every 600 s). It enqueues held issues updated since the last complete discovery, using the existing `_tbr_seed_reason` trust and eligibility check.

## Why

Observed on 2026-10-30 on a maintainer runner (v3.39.94):

- `last_seed_epoch` was dated 2026-10-20: no complete seed pass in 10 days. The registry has 68 pulse repos.
- In one managed private repository, 141 open issues matched the seed's second query (`label:"status:blocked" "Terminal blocker" in:comments`); the REST read returned 30. One owner-scoped query with five `user:` qualifiers returned all 154 fleet candidates in two pages.
- A read-only census of those 141 found 15 with an OWNER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` posted after the latest observation that were still `status:blocked`. Two of the 15 carried protected hold labels. Some retries dated back to 2026-10-07.
- After those issues were added to the local queue by hand, one `rearm` pass released 13 with `reason=trusted_retry`. A worker dispatched within about 6 minutes.
- Downstream impact: a repository automation posts up to three scheduled trusted retries and treats a retry as failed after 24 h of continued blocking. Because the retries were never applied, 51 issues in that repository were marked unavailable after three retries that never ran a worker.

`terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` documents that queue records are evidence, never authority. Release still re-verifies the trusted retry, the revision, hold labels and the public receipt. Faster intake therefore grants nothing new; it only applies existing re-arm decisions sooner.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-github.sh`
  - REST `terminal_blocker_search_issues`: add `--paginate -f per_page=100`, and treat `incomplete_results: true` as a failed read so the GraphQL fallback runs. Never accept a partial result as complete.
  - Add `terminal_blocker_search_issue_refs <query>`, which prints `owner/repo<TAB>number` lines. Use the same REST-first, GraphQL-fallback contract (`repository{nameWithOwner}`, fully paginated, any error means failure).
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
  - Add `tbr_discover_recent`. Build owner qualifiers (`user:<owner>`, in groups of at most 5) from the pulse repos in `repos.json`, using the same selector as `tbr_seed`. Search `is:issue is:open label:"status:blocked" "Terminal blocker" in:comments updated:>=<since>` and keep only registered pulse repos. Skip refs already in `queue/`. For the rest, fetch comments, apply `_tbr_seed_reason` (with the repo policy check and `policy_remote` intake exactly as in `tbr_seed`), and call `tbr_enqueue`.
  - `since` comes from a `last_discovery_epoch` stamp minus an overlap (default 900 s, for search-index lag). With no stamp, omit `updated:` so the first complete pass backfills every current hold.
  - Progress: save a `discovery_cursor` before each candidate, rotate with `_tbr_rotate` exactly as the seed does, and advance the stamp (and remove the cursor) only after a complete pass. A timed-out pass resumes and never stamps.
  - Run it as stage `discovery` at the start of `tbr_pending --rearm-only` through `_tbr_run_stage`, which keeps the existing per-stage cap. Allow it in the `_stage` dispatcher. Discovery failure marks the pass incomplete (rc 2) but must not skip the queue pass.
  - Update the header usage and env documentation.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-github.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`

## Acceptance

1. A REST search response with more than one page returns every item. `incomplete_results: true` falls back to GraphQL, and a failed fallback returns non-zero.

title: docs: Ghostscript advisory checks: CloudLinux 8 fix status and WordPress core PostScript refusal (CVE-2026-101258)
body:
## What

Add two short, observed facts to the image-library audit guidance, so the next Ghostscript advisory check is quick and does not lead to WordPress mitigations that core already provides.

## Why: evidence observed 2026-10-30 on a Hostinger Cloud account (CloudLinux 8)

- GHSA-g96p-c3cq-wp28 / CVE-2026-101258 (high, published 2026-10-06): a crafted PostScript or EPS file escapes Ghostscript's `-dSAFER` sandbox and runs shell commands.
- The host's Ghostscript 9.27 (`/usr/bin/gs`) was built 2026-10-06 and installed 2026-10-13 (the `stat` method already in `hostinger.md`).
- CloudLinux's changelog API, which `hostinger.md` already documents for `alt-ImageMagick`, answers for `ghostscript` too, but on 2026-10-30 listed only el7 builds (TuxCare ELS 9.25; this CVE fixed in `ghostscript-9.25-5.0.1.el7.tuxcare.els3`, 2026-10-21) and nothing for el8. Red Hat's CVE page (https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2026-101258) said RHEL 8's Ghostscript 9.27 was still under analysis. So on CloudLinux 8 the API cannot show the Ghostscript fix status: read Red Hat's CVE page for RHEL 8, then ask the host.
- With ImageMagick's open policy (only `Undefined`/`none`), plain `Imagick::readImage()` opened a PostScript file named `.jpg` as `PS`: ImageMagick detects the format from content, so Ghostscript ran.
- WordPress 7.1.4 closes that route in core:
  - `wp_check_filetype_and_ext()` rejected PostScript content named `photo.jpg` or `scan.pdf` (`ext=false`, `type=false`), and `.ps`/`.eps` are not allowed upload types.
  - `WP_Image_Editor_Imagick::load()` (`wp-includes/class-wp-image-editor-imagick.php`, comment "Reject files which Imagick will parse as PostScript") refuses PostScript signatures (`%!`, `\x04%!`, `\xC5\xD0\xD3\xC6`, `\xFFWPC`) and extensions, and `.pdf`/`.ai` files without `%PDF-`, before Imagick reads them. `wp_get_image_editor()` on a PostScript file named `.pdf` returned "File is not an image."
  - So, through WordPress's editor API, only genuine PDFs reach Ghostscript (thumbnails). Direct `new Imagick()` / `readImage()` callers in plugins bypass this check.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`
- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md`

## Files to modify

1. `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` → "Read-only audit notes" → **Shared image library** bullet: next to the sentence that lists the packages the CloudLinux changelog API answers for, and the Ghostscript sentence ("Ghostscript is `/usr/bin/gs` … ask the host whether the package carries later security fixes"), add that the API's `ghostscript` entries were el7/TuxCare only on 2026-10-30, so on CloudLinux 8 check Red Hat's CVE page for the RHEL 8 status and ask the host.
2. `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md` → "### Image-library advisories: who can reach it": add a short item (or extend item 1, "Trace processing, not storage") for Ghostscript/PostScript advisories: WordPress 7.1.4 core refuses PostScript before Imagick reads it (function and observed result above); ImageMagick detects the format from content, so direct `new Imagick($path)` / `readImage()` callers need their own checks. Find them with the existing grep (`new \\?Imagick`) and judge each by where its file comes from.

## Reference pattern

Follow the existing style of those sections: observed version and date, the command or function, the observed result, and a recheck caveat. Keep site names, account usernames and local paths out.

## Verification

- The repo's markdown lint passes on both files.
- Existing anchors still resolve (`hostinger.md#read-only-audit-notes` is linked from `wp-admin.md`).
- No private site names, usernames or local paths in the diff.

## Out of scope

No code changes. No extra WordPress mitigation for PostScript is recommended beyond core's check; the host fix remains the remedy.

title: fix(issue-sync): enrich erases appended brief/feedback sections and rewrites unchanged bodies
body:
## Problem

`issue-sync-helper.sh enrich` runs on every `TODO.md` push and rewrites every open plan-linked issue body. It erases content other automation appended after the signature footer, and it rewrites bodies that have not changed.

### Evidence (#36061, t18806)

1. 09:13 / 10:26 UTC: brief repair and merge-pass conflict routing appended `### Files Scope`, `### Worker Guidance`, `### Verification`, integration scope evidence and the `feedback-route:start/complete:conflict:PR36066:SHA…` section after the footer (body 4871 chars).
2. 15:03:50 UTC, run `41076975933` (push of TODO.md for t18808): `Enriched #36061 (t18806)`, body replaced by the 757-char TODO stub. All appended content and the feedback-route completion marker were lost.
3. The same run reports `Enrich complete: 7 updated (9/9 processed)`. 16:05 rewrote #36061 again with only a footer version change.
4. Each rewrite changes the terminal-blocker task revision (`{title, body}` hash), so the `input_required` hold observed at 10:43 was released at 15:30 as `revision_changed`. The task is now dispatchable with no brief, and its next worker will block again.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-enrich.sh` `_enrich_update_issue`:

- Case 3 (no brief file, sync sentinel present) and case 2 (brief file present) treat the whole body as owned by issue-sync. Anything after the `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` footer belongs to other writers (feedback routes, brief repairs, scope evidence) and is discarded.
- The no-op check compares `current_body == composed`. `compose_issue_body` produces no footer, while every stored body carries the wrapper-appended footer, so the check never matches and every enrich rewrites every signed body.

## Fix

- Split the stored body at its first signature footer (`<!-- aidevops:origin:* -->` + `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` + `---` + version line) into the synced head, the footer and an appended tail.
- Cases 2/3: skip the write when the head already equals the composed body (ignoring trailing whitespace), so unchanged issues are not rewritten and footer version churn stops.
- When the head differs, write `composed + existing footer + appended tail`, so appended sections survive and keep the order other writers rely on.
- `FORCE_ENRICH` keeps its documented full-replace semantics; case 4 (external body) is unchanged.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-enrich.sh` — `_enrich_update_issue` plus new body-split helpers.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-brief-inline-classifier.sh` / `test-enrich-no-data-loss.sh` — existing `_enrich_update_issue` suites to keep passing; add focused cases for tail preservation and footer-only no-op.

## Verification

- Existing enrich suites pass; ShellCheck clean.
- New cases: signed unchanged body → no write; changed head with tail → composed + footer + tail; no footer → old behaviour; FORCE_ENRICH → full replace.
- After release: the next TODO.md push logs `Body unchanged` for unchanged plan-linked issues instead of `Enriched`.

## Follow-up in scope

Restore the #36061 brief from its 10:26 revision so t18806 is dispatchable with full context.

## Reproducer

`gh api graphql` `userContentEdits` on #36061 shows the 4871-char body at 10:26:07 replaced by github-actions at 15:03:47; run `41076975933` log line 537 `Enriched #36061 (t18806)`.

title: docs(wordpress): site mail over own SMTP/IMAP, never a vendor hosted relay
body:
## What

Add the owner's site-mail data-privacy policy to the WordPress guidance:

- Send outbound site mail through the site's SMTP plugin (FluentSMTP) to the owner's own mail provider.
- Read inbound support mail from the owner's own mailbox over IMAP. For Fluent Support, use SEO Pro Stack's "Fluent Support email by IMAP" or whichever plugin manages the mailbox.
- Never route customer email through a vendor's hosted relay or piping service. Fluent Support Pro's email piping is one example: its hosted relay receives every email and forwards it only to licensed sites.
- A GPL feature that can run locally must not wait on a licence check or call-home. Call the plugin's own local code instead.

## Why

Customer email is personal data, and a relay gives a third party a copy of every message. The relay is also unnecessary: SEO Pro Stack 1.3.118 reads the mailbox over IMAP and passes each email to Fluent Support Pro's own `ByMailHandler::processPayload()`, so tickets are created on the site. That path was verified live on the support site.

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #35605 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #35605

**Parent issue:** #35605 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** Dispatch: fix dominant precreate.* sub-stage tail for large repos under concurrent dispatch (follow-up to #35602)
**Parent labels:** `bug,status:available,auto-dispatch,priority:medium,tier:thinking,origin:worker,consolidation-in-progress`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #35605 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available`, never the parent's lifecycle status. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #35605:**

```bash
gh issue comment 35605 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 35605 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 35605 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 35605 $NEW_NUM
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #35605 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #35605.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What

Fix the dominant `precreate_worktree` tail sub-stage for large repositories under concurrent dispatch, using the `precreate.*` sub-stage records added for #35602.

#35602 added the publication reserve (no more publish-then-abort) and sub-stage timing, but deliberately did not change worktree creation: the issue required the contention hypothesis to be confirmed with data first. Those records only exist after the change is deployed and several dispatch cycles have run, so the tail fix is split out here.

## Why

On one maintainer host (2026-10-22 to 2026-10-25), `precreate_worktree` for a large monorepo (about 16k tracked files, 580 MiB packs, 35 unrepacked packs, about 5,800 loose objects, 30+ linked worktrees) measured p50 / p90 / max = 40.0 / 142.5 / 353.9 s (n=185). An uncontended `git fetch --no-tags origin <default>` took 4.3 s, so fetch alone does not explain the tail. That tail, together with claim consensus, uses up most of the 300 s prelaunch budget.

## Precondition (check first)

Run `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dispatch-stage-instrument.sh report 86400` on the runner. If there are fewer than about 30 `precreate.helper_add` records, the data is not ready yet. In that case stop, citing this precondition, and use `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=external_trigger_pending`. Do not guess the dominant stage.

## Reproducer

Unconfirmed investigation: the tail has been observed, but its cause still needs the new data.

1. Dispatch three or four batch issues from the same large repository in one pulse cycle. Each creates a fresh worktree concurrently against one object store.
2. `dispatch-stage-instrument.sh report 86400` then shows `precreate_worktree` p90 above 140 s and bursts of `pre_runtime_failure:prelaunch_budget_exhausted` (15 of the last 20 came from that repository).
3. With #35602 deployed, the same report also lists `precreate.*` rows; the largest p90 among them is the stage to fix.

## How

1. Compare p50/p90/max for each `precreate.*` stage (see `.agents/reference/dispatch-timing.md` "Worktree pre-creation sub-stages"). Nested stages overlap: `precreate.create_worktree` contains `base_fetch`, `sibling_status`, `scratch_add`, the remote checks, `registry_*` and `git_worktree_add`. `precreate.helper_add` minus the helper's own stages gives the helper startup cost. `precreate_worktree` minus `helper_add` and `restore_deps` gives the dispatcher-side reuse selection and registration cost.
2. Group the records by concurrent attempts (the timestamps overlap within the same pulse cycle) to confirm or rule out object-store contention.
3. Fix the dominant sub-stage. Candidate directions, to choose from the data rather than in advance:
   - `git_worktree_add`/`scratch_add`: a full checkout of a 16k-file tree, which competes under concurrency. Options are a per-repo creation lock or limiting concurrency to one or two per repo, or a sparse/no-checkout scratch worktree for the fresh-base fetch.
   - `base_fetch`: when several creations run at once, reuse one fresh `origin/<default>` refresh per repo per cycle.
   - `sibling_status`: a status probe on a large index. Use a cheaper health probe or cap the number of probes.
   - `restore_deps`/`helper_deps`/`preview_routes`: skip or defer anything not needed before spawn.
4. Keep RAM-only dispatch policy. Do not add CPU-load, idle or core-count gating. Do not change the prelaunch deadline, the publication reserve, lease TTL arithmetic or orphan grace.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-worktree-create.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/scratch-worktree-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`
- `.agents/reference/dispatch-timing.md`

The exact files depend on which sub-stage dominates. Paths outside this list follow `reference/worker-discipline.md` "Integration scope recovery".

## Acceptance

- The PR description includes the per-stage p50/p90/max table that shows the dominant sub-stage.
- After deploy, the large-repo `precreate_worktree` p90 measurably falls on the same host, compared with the 142.5 s baseline.
- No new CPU/idle gating, and no change to deadline, reserve or lease semantics.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on the changed scripts.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-prelaunch-publication-reserve.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-fresh-base.sh`
- After deploy: `dispatch-stage-instrument.sh report 86400`, comparing `precreate_worktree` and the dominant `precreate.*` stage before and after.

Ref #35602

title: consolidated: fix measured precreate worktree tail under concurrent dispatch
body:
_Supersedes #35605 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Fix the dominant `precreate_worktree` tail sub-stage for large repositories under concurrent dispatch, using the `precreate.*` sub-stage records added for #35602.

#35602 added the publication reserve (no more publish-then-abort) and sub-stage timing, but deliberately did not change worktree creation: the contention hypothesis first required deployed data over several dispatch cycles. This successor owns the measured tail fix, not a predetermined optimization.

## Why

On one maintainer host (2026-10-22 to 2026-10-25), `precreate_worktree` for a large monorepo (about 16k tracked files, 580 MiB packs, 35 unrepacked packs, about 5,800 loose objects, 30+ linked worktrees) measured p50 / p90 / max = 40.0 / 142.5 / 353.9 s (n=185). An uncontended `git fetch --no-tags origin <default>` took 4.3 s, so fetch alone does not explain the tail. Together with claim consensus, this uses most of the 300 s prelaunch budget.

## Runner prerequisites and precondition

Run `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dispatch-stage-instrument.sh report 86400` on the implementation runner. Require about 30 `precreate.helper_add` records. Per @marcusquinn's 2026-10-30 07:17 update, use `report 259200` (72 hours) if the 24-hour window is short. If the runner still has fewer than about 30 records, stop, cite the observed window/count, and use `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=runner_capability_unmet`: the records are runner-local, so this keeps the issue available for a runner that has them (the maintainer runner did on 2026-10-30). Do not use `external_trigger_pending` or `input_required` for this (#36133). Do not guess the dominant stage. Use the implementing runner's own raw records for concurrency grouping.

The maintainer runner met the precondition on 2026-10-30 (~19:00 UTC: 35 records in 24 hours); this supersedes a blanket claim that data is not ready, not the requirement for sufficient local records. No source brief declares a `requires-secrets:` prerequisite.

## Reproducer

Unconfirmed investigation: the tail has been observed, but its cause still needs raw-record analysis.

1. Dispatch three or four batch issues from the same large repository in one pulse cycle. Each creates a fresh worktree concurrently against one object store.
2. `dispatch-stage-instrument.sh report 86400` originally showed `precreate_worktree` p90 above 140 s and bursts of `pre_runtime_failure:prelaunch_budget_exhausted` (15 of the last 20 came from that repository).
3. With #35602 deployed, the report also lists `precreate.*` rows; the largest p90 among inner stages is the stage to investigate, accounting for wrapper overlap.

## How

1. Compare p50/p90/max for every `precreate.*` stage; read `.agents/reference/dispatch-timing.md`, "Worktree pre-creation sub-stages". Nested stages overlap: `precreate.create_worktree` contains `base_fetch`, `sibling_status`, `scratch_add`, remote checks, `registry_*` and `git_worktree_add`. `precreate.helper_add` minus the helper's stages estimates helper startup cost. `precreate_worktree` minus `helper_add` and `restore_deps` estimates dispatcher-side reuse selection and registration cost. Use raw attempt durations for residual attribution rather than treating subtraction of aggregate percentiles as an exact measurement.
2. Group runner-local raw records by concurrent attempts (overlapping timestamps within the same pulse cycle) to confirm or rule out object-store contention. The supplied aggregate tables do not establish causation or supply p90 for every stage.
3. Fix the dominant sub-stage. Choose among these candidate directions from data, not in advance:
   - `git_worktree_add`/`scratch_add`: a full checkout of a 16k-file tree competes under concurrency. Consider a per-repo creation lock, creation concurrency limited to one or two per repo, or a sparse/no-checkout scratch worktree for fresh-base fetch.
   - `base_fetch`: reuse one fresh `origin/<default>` refresh per repo per cycle when several creations run concurrently.
   - `sibling_status`: use a cheaper health probe or cap the number of probes on large indexes.
   - `restore_deps`/`helper_deps`/`preview_routes`: skip or defer work not needed before spawn. Include generation verification, exclusions and startup when investigating helper-side overhead.
4. Reference locations verified in the consolidation worktree (recheck after updating): `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh:1169` (sibling probe), `:1185` (scratch), `:1194` (fetch), `:1283` (create), `:1574` (dependencies), `:1586` (preview routes); `.agents/scripts/shared-worktree-create.sh:68` (native add); `.agents/scripts/scratch-worktree-helper.sh:151` (`scratch_worktree_add`); `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:881` (dispatcher precreation), `:937` (helper timing); `.agents/reference/dispatch-timing.md:58` (stage documentation). Choose minimal changes matching the measured stage and keep documentation accurate.
5. Keep RAM-only dispatch policy. Do not add CPU-load, idle or core-count gating. Do not change the prelaunch deadline, publication reserve, lease TTL arithmetic or orphan grace.
6. Exact changed files depend on the dominant sub-stage. Paths outside this list follow `reference/worker-discipline.md` "Integration scope recovery" before editing.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-worktree-create.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/scratch-worktree-helper.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh
- EDIT: .agents/reference/dispatch-timing.md
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh (stub git: emit porcelain for reuse fixtures; required by the listed verification)

_Integration scope recovery (worker, 2026-10-30): the implementing runner's raw records attribute the largest leaf p90 to dispatcher-side reuse selection (`precreate_worktree` start to `helper_add` start: p50 2.9 s / p90 6.3 s / max 23.9 s, n=475). That code is `_dlw_select_issue_worktree` in `pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh`, sourced by `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`; no open PR or claimed issue touches it._

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Sufficient runner-local samples are verified (24 hours, or 72 hours if needed); raw concurrency grouping confirms or rules out contention before selecting a fix.
- [ ] The PR description includes the per-stage p50/p90/max table showing the dominant sub-stage, accounting for overlapping wrappers and helper overhead.
- [ ] The measured dominant sub-stage is optimized, not a presumed cause.
- [ ] After deploy, large-repo `precreate_worktree` p90 measurably falls on the same host against the 142.5 s baseline; record total and dominant-stage before/after comparisons.
- [ ] No CPU/idle/core-count gating or changes to deadline, publication reserve, lease TTL arithmetic or orphan grace.
- [ ] Focused verification below passes.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on changed scripts.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-prelaunch-publication-reserve.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-fresh-base.sh`
- After deploy: `dispatch-stage-instrument.sh report 86400`, comparing `precreate_worktree` and the dominant `precreate.*` stage before/after on the same host. Disclose the window; use 72 hours if needed for sufficient samples.

## Context & Decisions

Per @marcusquinn at 2026-10-30 07:17:21Z, the 2026-10-25 03:27Z `external_trigger_pending` hold was correct at the time: #35602 had closed six minutes earlier, so no sub-stage records yet existed. By 2026-10-30 07:20Z, `report 259200` on the maintainer runner showed:

| Stage | p50 | p95 | p99 | n |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `dedup.precreate_worktree` | 33.1 s | 204.7 s | 302.6 s | 194 |
| `precreate.helper_add` | 29.7 s | 189.5 s | 282.3 s | 187 |
| `precreate.create_worktree` | 16.3 s | 113.9 s | 168.6 s | 188 |
| `precreate.git_worktree_add` | 5.0 s | 59.9 s | 94.7 s | 189 |
| `precreate.verify_generation` | 3.7 s | 33.9 s | 53.4 s | 184 |
| `precreate.helper_deps` | 4.5 s | 22.9 s | 29.7 s | 184 |
| `precreate.sibling_status` | 2.8 s | 22.7 s | 30.3 s | 186 |

The 24-hour window had 26 helper samples, versus 187 over 72 hours, so use the larger window when short. Per @marcusquinn, `helper_add` wraps nested stages: attribute its tail to the inner stage with largest p90 (initial start point: `create_worktree`, then `git_worktree_add`) rather than the wrapper. Compare same-host before/after total p90 against 142.5 s.

Per @marcusquinn at 2026-10-30 18:57:49Z, the 07:58 hold was a pre-v3.39.94 `reason=unknown` exit from a runner without records. It was not evidence of a globally unmet trigger. The maintainer runner's 24-hour report at ~19:00 UTC showed n=35 helper samples:

| Stage | p50 | p95 | max | n |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `precreate_worktree` | 29.3 s | 79.0 s | 91.2 s | 38 |
| `precreate.helper_add` | 26.6 s | 66.7 s | 85.2 s | 35 |
| `precreate.create_worktree` | 14.8 s | 32.8 s | 36.4 s | 35 |
| `precreate.git_worktree_add` | 2.2 s | 8.8 s | 11.2 s | 36 |
| `precreate.registry_begin_create` | 0.1 s | 8.0 s | 10.4 s | 36 |
| `precreate.preview_routes` | 3.7 s | 11.0 s | 12.6 s | 32 |
| `precreate.verify_generation` | 3.3 s | 9.5 s | 17.2 s | 32 |
| `precreate.helper_deps` | 3.9 s | 7.3 s | 8.7 s | 32 |
| `precreate.sibling_status` | 1.5 s | 4.6 s | 5.0 s | 33 |
| `precreate.base_fetch` | 1.8 s | 3.4 s | 3.8 s | 35 |

Per @marcusquinn, `helper_add` minus `create_worktree` leaves roughly 12 s p50 / 34 s p95 helper-side cost: dependencies, preview routes, generation verification, exclusions and startup. That gap is larger than fetch or `git worktree add` alone. Treat this as an investigation lead; use own raw records for grouping, and retain the local sample precondition. Both maintainer updates requested `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry`.

Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable. No checkpoint commit or branch is prescribed by these sources.

Ref #35602. Consolidation task: #36128. This successor is the implementation handoff; consolidation itself makes no code or performance claim.

## Tier

`tier:thinking` (preserved): dispatch-path changes and a data-dependent concurrency/optimization decision remain.
